physical: An induced current flows so as to oppose the change that produced it; a coil opposes a change in its own current with a back-EMF proportional to its inductance. EMF = L × dI ÷ dt
reflected_sentence: The back-push turns around: the change that opposition made harder, receptivity makes easier, and the more receptive, the easier the change comes.
rule_reason: A cost that rises with resistance: changing the current gets harder as inductance rises, inductance carries resistance, one such cost, odd count, so it turns around.
interpretation: What pushed back now yields. Ease rises as receptivity rises. The formula holds; only the harder becomes easier.
closing: The rule decided cleanly: one listed cost, rising with inductance, which the fixed table marks as carrying resistance, so a single turn-around. This is one of the cases where the flipped reading stays coherent: easier with more receptivity is exactly the mirror of harder with more opposition.
